# FlairUp

FlairUp is a lightweight CSS-in-JS library for UI package authors
(React, Vue, framework-agnostic). Version documented here: 1.1.x.
Repository: https://github.com/ealush/flairup
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/flairup
Docs: https://ealush.github.io/flairup

## When to use it

Use FlairUp when shipping reusable UI components whose styles must work
without consumer setup: no CSS files to import, no bundler plugins, no
framework-specific SSR handling. Not a general app-styling framework.

## Install

npm install flairup

## API (five functions)

createSheet(name, rootNode?)
  Creates a named stylesheet. Returns { create, keyframes, getStyle }.
  rootNode: an element to mount into, null for strings-only (SSR), or
  omitted to mount into <head>.

sheet.create(styles)
  Defines named scopes of camelCase declarations. Each scope returns a
  Set with one class per declaration. Supports :hover / ::before,
  .parent markers, &.compound selectors, @media queries, nested
  conditions, a -- block of CSS variables, and . for passthrough
  classes. Example:
    const styles = sheet.create({
      card: {
        padding: '16px',
        '--accent': '#a31621',
        '&:hover': { borderColor: 'var(--accent)' },
        '@media (min-width: 700px)': { padding: '24px' },
      },
    });

cx(...args)
  Combines class Sets, strings, arrays, and { className: boolean }
  maps into one class string for className. Example:
    cx(styles.card, isActive && styles.active, extraClass)

sheet.keyframes(frames)
  Defines animations; returns names for the animation property.
  Example:
    const { fadeIn } = sheet.keyframes({
      fadeIn: { from: { opacity: '0' }, to: { opacity: '1' } },
    });

sheet.getStyle()
  Returns the whole stylesheet as CSS text. SSR pattern: create the
  sheet with a null root on the server, inject the string into a
  <style> tag. The same calls run unchanged in the browser.

## Rules for generated code

- Style objects use camelCase properties with string values.
- Reference classes only through the Sets returned by create(); never
  hardcode generated class names (they are content hashes).
- Keep one sheet per package (createSheet('my-package')) and compose
  with cx() at the call site.
- Conditions nest arbitrarily; keep them next to the declarations
  they modify.
